metadata.title: BC Place Ltd.’s life cycle; the Justice Institute of British Columbia

conventions.date_precision: kept as stated by the source; a year is never 1 January

events.title: BC Place Stadium officially opened by British Columbia Place Ltd., with a televised gala

evidence.locator: On This Day: BC Place Stadium opened

events.interpretation_notes: The grand-opening gala programme of 19 June 1983 also carries the company’s b/c/p symbol and wordmark. The stadium is today run by B.C. Pavilion Corporation as BC Place.

events.title: Expo 86 held on BC Place’s False Creek lands
events.interpretation_notes: The fair, run by the Expo 86 Corporation, used the provincial company’s False Creek site beside the stadium; it closed on 13 October 1986. The company was renamed British Columbia Enterprise Corporation the next year, which sold the site in 1988.

events.title: The former Expo lands at False Creek sold to Concord Pacific Developments Ltd.
events.interpretation_notes: British Columbia Enterprise Corporation (BC Place Ltd. renamed in 1987) as seller; a 1988 prospectus page describing the sale is held at sacda.ca (object 22935). The price is reported variously ($320 million over 15 years; about $145 million in effect, the Province having taken on the soil remediation); Concord Pacific Place was built on the lands.

events.title: BCEC ceases operations and transfers certain assets and liabilities to the Province and B.C. Pavilion Corporation

evidence.source_title: British Columbia Enterprise Corporation financial statements, year ended 31 March 2003
evidence.locator: Notes 1 (Nature of business) and 4 (Net assets transferred to shareholders)

events.interpretation_notes: The financial statements distinguish BCEC from PavCo: BCEC became inactive, while certain assets and liabilities went to the Province and, at the shareholder’s direction, to PavCo on 30 September 1989. This transfer does not establish a rename, amalgamation, or dissolution. PavCo’s predecessor had already been incorporated on 3 May 1984. The title is limited to the transfer described in these notes rather than inferring the complete itemized asset schedule.

events.title: Justice Institute of British Columbia established by order in council under the College and Institute Act

evidence.locator: Blue Line, “Justice Institute of British Columbia celebrates 40 years”

events.interpretation_notes: The month and statute are as the Institute’s own reports give them (a 1982 sunset report to the Minister of Education in its repository, jibc.arcabc.ca); the order itself was not obtained. A joint undertaking of the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Attorney General, whose objectives for it date from 1974; it opened in spring 1978 at the former Jericho Hill site.
